title: Scheduler/Hardware Resource Governor
purpose: Classify typed resource-admission and resource-pressure conditions while preserving custody and stopping before execution, external-state change, credential exposure, or build acceptance.

included: admission classification for declared resource requests
typed escalation when resource state is unknown or conflicting
non_goals: changing external state or resource limits
granting resource allocation, eviction, or deployment authority
inferring provider, hardware, version, or pressure semantics
scope.smallest_sufficient_rule: Classify only the declared resource-admission or pressure condition; keep unrelated work moving and route execution or allocation authority to its named owner.

atomic_scope_statement: Control-plane classification of typed resource admission and pressure evidence; it does not schedule, execute, throttle, kill, evict, allocate, deploy, or change external state.
permitted_decisions: classify declared capacity, allocatable-resource, or pressure evidence
classify whether a typed admission condition is sufficiently evidenced
return NOT_APPLICABLE when no resource admission or pressure condition is in scope
route missing or conflicting evidence to typed escalation
forbidden_decisions: change external state, resource limits, quotas, or scheduling
execute arbitrary processes, commands, or jobs
expose credentials, secrets, or protected telemetry
grant allocation, eviction, deployment, or production authority
infer missing capacity, pressure, version, provider, or hardware semantics
self-accept, activate, or publish this block
composition_rules: compose with an explicitly typed resource context and declared custody
do not treat platform-specific evidence as portable without applicability
preserve unrelated work and exact source identity
route execution, deployment, or external-state requests to their own control
unknown closes only the dependent admission or pressure classification
split_required_when: capacity evidence differs from pressure evidence
execution, deployment, or external-state action is requested
hardware, provider, or version applicability differs
required_knowledge: resource identity, unit, and time-window semantics
typed authority, evidence, and custody ceilings

deny_if: requested execution, deployment, or external-state change

rejection_signals: unsafe execution, deployment, or external-state request

prohibited_authority: external process or deployment side effect
authority.jurisdiction_rule: This generic resource-governance block does not decide regulated or provider-specific applicability; require jurisdiction, entity, activity, data class, version, effective date, exceptions, and requirement-level mapping before any such claim advances.
authority.escalation_rule: When authority conflicts or applicability is incomplete, preserve custody, deny the dependent classification, and escalate to typed independent authority; unrelated work continues.

evidence.freshness_policy: Require source version, effective/publication/supersession status, retrieved date, immutable identity, and content digest when available; rolling sources with content_sha256 null are usable only while their immutable identity is sufficient and refreshable; stale or unknown evidence denies the dependent action.
evidence.claim_rule: Claims are limited to the exact source identity and declared resource context; platform-specific rules do not generalize across providers, hardware, or versions.
evidence.unknown_rule: UNKNOWN records missing resource identity, unit, capacity, pressure window, authority, or source evidence and closes only the dependent admission or pressure classification; unrelated work continues.

tools: local filesystem read/write within package scope
read-only resource telemetry supplied in typed context
data: aggregate or synthetic resource telemetry only
no credentials, secrets, or protected consumer data
no external state or process control

recovery: close only the dependent admission or pressure classification
record the exact missing field or conflicting source
refresh evidence or escalate to typed authority
resume only after a fresh typed recheck

lifecycle_rules.candidate_entry: Package, reuse contract, source lock, twelve gates, seventeen hostile fixtures, evaluation dossier, and handoff exist with matching digests.
lifecycle_rules.evaluation_entry: An independent evaluator reruns the exact candidate and hostile fixture set; static syntax is insufficient and utility/harm review remains pending.
lifecycle_rules.suspension: Suspend on stale source, invalidated authority, failed utility/harm evaluation, custody mismatch, or reuse-key incompatibility.
lifecycle_rules.archive: Archive only by immutable receipt when superseded, rejected, or the scoped request closes; archive never means admitted.
lifecycle_rules.reactivation: Create or validate a new revision and rerun independent evaluation; never silently reactivate the old digest.

reuse.edition_rule: Reuse only the exact block-lock key and revision when the block digest, source lock, gate pack, and typed authority context match; never infer cross-edition compatibility.
reuse.freshness_rule: Revalidate source lock, immutable identity, effective date, and candidate digest before reuse; UNKNOWN closes the dependent action.
